messages:
Lena (AE): Helios POC: customer ran a burst-sim warmup with 60 parallel clients. They're seeing 2-3s TTFT spikes and periodic 429s. Can SE/SRE triage? :thinking_face:
Jonah (SE): Oof. Which runtime/model and are they using prefetch? Any client config?
Lena (AE): Model: helios-13b-fp16, typical prompt ~300 tokens, peak 800. Client used batch=24, prefetch=true, and they did an aggressive global prefetch script.
Tomas (ML): Prefetch + global parallelism + large batch is a known pattern for cache thrash. Also check if they hit router egress limits — we saw similar with multi-tenant egress policing.
Priya (SRE): Looking at infra: tenant egress was near 95% for a short window at 2045012200; our router ingress queue showed backlog and gateway returned 429s from per-tenant concurrency gate. Also saw repeated KV shard evictions at 2045012215 which will kill prefix cache hits.
Jonah (SE): KV shard evictions? Why would prefetch cause evictions?
Tomas (ML): If many clients prefetch different prefixes, shard working set grows and LRU evicts frequently. Combined with memory-pressure from large batch decoding, we get cache churn and worse TTFT.
Lena (AE): Customer insisted they needed the high parallelism to simulate spikes. They asked if Dedicated would avoid this.
Priya (SRE): Dedicated reduces noisy neighbor egress and gives isolated cache shards, but it doesn't magically remove bad warmup patterns. For POC short-term fixes: 1) stop simultaneous client prefetch; 2) set batch.max_requests to 8 or 12; 3) enable streaming=true so first bytes return earlier.
Jonah (SE): Suggested client patch (small snippet):
```json
{"batch": {"max_requests": 12, "max_delay_ms": 8}, "prefetch": "staged", "stream": true}
```
Lena (AE): "staged" prefetch — what's that?
Tomas (ML): Use our /v1/prefetch?mode=staged that sequences prefetch by shard. Alternatively, orchestrate clients to stagger prefetch with a jittered sleep. Avoid all-clients one-shot.
Priya (SRE): I can temporarily bump their tenant concurrency cap from 30 -> 48 for 90 minutes while they replay a controlled burst. I'll also pin their service to the less-loaded egress rack. :white_check_mark:
QuokkaBot: alert/tenant/helios-poc: increased concurrency cap applied at 2045012300 by Priya (SRE). Monitoring enabled.
Jonah (SE): Also instrument a trace: ask them to include X-Trace-Id header and capture gateway/router/runtime timing. Prefer a few traces: one during warmup and one during steady-state.
Lena (AE): They also want a handwritten estimate for Dedicated monthly starting point to justify ask. Anything we can share now?
Priya (SRE): Quick thumb: 8xA100 equivalent Dedicated pod ~ ~$Yk/month baseline plus premium for private egress. But for POC we can offer a short trial of a pre-warmed Dedicated node with temporary uplift; Sales Ops will need to formalize.
Jonah (SE): For presales messaging: "Hosted + tuned warmup (staggered prefetch + small batch + streaming) is typically cheapest for POC. Dedicated gives predictable latency under sustained heavy concurrency and isolates egress and cache pressure."
Tomas (ML): Also note quantization path: if they switch to fp4/approx quant we need to re-measure per-token decode cost at long context; can increase tail latency.
Lena (AE): Action items: 1) ask customer to run staged prefetch (+ jitter), set batch.max_requests=12 and stream=true; 2) provide 3 traces (warmup+steady+spike); 3) Priya will open temporary concurrency bump and monitor; 4) I'll flag Sales Ops for Dedicated trial quote.
Priya (SRE): I'll watch eviction rate and queue depth; will rollback bump if noisy neighbor risk increases.
Lena (AE): Thanks team, I'll send the config and example curl to the customer and request traces. Re-open if they still hit 429s or TTFT > 1s. :raised_hands:
